notes.note: A pashta is a post-fix accent. The shift from a qadma accent to a pasha accent requires a leftward shift of the symbol by one half of the letter's width. It's NOT perceptible with some fonts.

notes.note: This Decalogue text contains double accent, the text is also in poor condition. The mark in question is a broken line coming out of the rightmost leg of the sin. A pashta is post-positive and appears on the left side of the letter. One or two pashtas can occur on a word. If a word has a single pashta, it must occur on the final letter of the word. If a word has two pashtas, one occurs on the final letter and the other acts as an "accent helper" placed over the accented letter. This word has a single, pashta/qadma-like mark over the sin and no corresponding mark on the final letter. Therefore, the mark in question isn't a pashta, but a qadma,

BHL has a qadma centered over the sin. (Dotan numbers the division differently than the UXLC and other modern texts. He combines UXLC verses 6 and 7 into a single verse so that UXLC verse 8 is BHL verse 7.) BHLA has no entry for this verse.

notes.note: At question is the reddish upper dot of an apparent zaqef-qatan over the yod/vav. Two approaches are available, the first assumes the dot was once deliberately placed by the scribe. The first approach says that the reddish dot is probably the upper dot of a zaqaf-qatan over the yod displaced because of interference from a merkha from a word, סַלֵּ֥י, on the previous line. The second approach says the reddish dot is an anomaly unintended by the scribe, leaving a single dot over both the yod and the vav. A single dot over the yod would need to be a revia and second dot on the vav would be a holam. This transcription prefers the first approach because of a lack of other reddish dots in the sheet containing the text and the fact the dot is well-placed and well-sized. Also, the second approach's dot over the yod has no outstanding revia characteristics, such as a diamond shape. A note 't' is added, however.
BHL has a zaqaf-qatan over the yod. BHLA has no entry for this verse.
